head: gc-quarantine-r3
report:
Running the focused tests covering both prior findings.

I found no defects at this head. Both findings from the earlier round (astra, against head `09a15364`) are closed: the code no longer has either flaw, and the focused regression tests for both pass.

NO DEFECTS

## NOT A DEFECT

**Earlier finding 1 (P2): an unreadable quarantine directory was reported as "No place holds a whole copy". Closed.**
- **What changed:** `readQuarantinePlace` (`session-archive.ts:1828-1868`) used to stop when `readdir` failed. It now records `place.unreadable` and still looks for the record at its fixed name.
  - If the directory can be searched but not listed (mode `0100`), the `lstat`/open of the copy succeeds and the copy is found. The message then says to copy the record back, and to make the directory listable first (the `listFirst` text at 1942-1947).
  - If the directory can't be searched either (`0000`), the `lstat` fails with `EACCES`. `readRegularText` turns that into `copyUnreadable`, so the message says the copy could not be read, not that there is none.
- **When the "none to put back" text can still appear:** only when no copy was found and nothing failed to read. In a directory that can be searched, `ENOENT` at the record's name really means it is absent. A quarantine only ever writes the copy at that name, so the claim is true there.
- **Tests:** the three shapes (`0100`, `0000`, and `0000` next to a readable place holding the copy) are covered in `test/session-archive.test.ts:6148-6209`, for both preview and apply. They also follow the copy-back step through to `moved: true`.

**Earlier finding 2 (P2): a read failure during comparison was reported as "holds what … does not". Closed.**
- `archivedHandleIsHeldBy` (`session-archive.ts:2557-2577`) and `sourceIsPrefixOfDestination` (503-560) have no catch-all, so a read error propagates.
- Every reclaim/archive comparison caller in `gc-cli.ts` (lines 1237, 1808, 1896, 1996, 2119, 2153) wraps it in the new `compared()` (1160-1166). That rethrows the error as "X could not be compared with Y: …", keeping the cause.
- The one comparison left unwrapped is `handleBeginsWith` at `gc-cli.ts:1540`. An error there still propagates; nothing turns it into a false result.
- `publishedIsStaged` still returns false when a check fails. The earlier round accepted that as a deliberate exclusion, and I agree.
- Tests at `test/session-archive.test.ts:4022-4235` inject `EIO`/`EACCES` and expect "could not be compared" with both files unchanged.

**Test run:** `bun test test/session-archive.test.ts -t "quarantine|compared|comparison|read fails"` in `packages/coding-agent` at this head gave 60 pass, 0 fail, 490 `expect()` calls, in 12.5 s.

**Suspicions I ruled out:**
- **Corrupt `.jsonl.gz` at the archive destination:** `archiveAlreadyHolds` and `archiveIsPrefixOfLive` now throw "could not be compared" instead of reporting "holds a different session". That is the intended contract, and either way the run refuses and both copies survive.
- **A directory that can't be listed but holds only a partial copy of the record:** no whole copy, no read error, so "none to put back" is accurate.
- **Destination is a regular file:** `readdir` fails with `ENOTDIR` and the place is reported as "could not be listed (ENOTDIR)". The child `lstat` also gets `ENOTDIR`, which counts as nothing there. Accurate.
- **`session-arg.ts`:** `materializeSessionFile` runs after the `access` check on the explicit-path and id branches. With no argument, it still returns the most recent live session as before.

**Not covered:** there is no snapshot of the earlier head (`09a15364`) and the snapshot has no git, so I couldn't isolate this round's changes. I read the areas the earlier findings named, plus their callers.
